after_step.derivation: The objection is correct that the quoted step names pre-registered criteria without deriving them. I take it up by supplying question-relation criteria that do not depend on an answer key. A problem-posing correction is an edit that changes the question being answered: at least one of the requested decision or target, scope, assumptions, constraints, definitions, outcome measures, success conditions, or required form of answer. An answer-content edit changes only recommendations, explanations, predictions, evidence, or wording while those question elements remain fixed. In disputed cases, judges code these observable relations, not whether the revised advice is substantively correct. Use multiple judges blind to arm, pre-register the criteria, retain disagreements, adjudicate by majority or a third judge, and report reliability. This keeps the paired case-level comparison: same disputed prompt, one arm one-shot advice, one arm other-model questioning plus revision; keep original prompt, initial advice, critiques, revised advice, and blind adjudication of each candidate edit. Competing explanations for any arm difference can be distinguished by coding total edit volume, answer-content-only edits, and text length; genuine posing-correction advantage must survive those comparisons. If advice does not change, that can mean no candidate posing mistake was detected, or that critique/revision failed to elicit a correction; examine whether critics raised candidate posing issues and whether the reviser acted on them.
after_step.result:
